feedback: The UI changes largely meet the requirements (title in header only, date picker icon inside the Date field, spacing, and conditional Scan receipt button). However, the usage of PrimaryButton with an unsupported "variant" prop will break the app and cause test failures when the component is rendered. Fix the button usage to match the actual PrimaryButton API, or replace it with a component that supports a text‐style button. Once corrected, re‑run the test suite to ensure all acceptance and unit tests still pass.
unproven: PrimaryButton component does not accept a "variant" prop. In ReceiptEntryScreen.tsx the code uses <PrimaryButton label="Looks right" variant="text" onPress={...} />, which will cause a runtime error or prop type mismatch. Verify the PrimaryButton component's API and adjust the code: either use a different button component that supports a text variant (e.g., TextButton) or remove the variant prop.

The "Looks right" button is rendered inside a <View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}> alongside the FormField, but the button's testID is not defined. If tests need to interact with it, add a testID attribute to the button.
open_notes: R1 violation: The screen title "Add receipt" appears twice as a literal string in the screen component source (comment and comments) – the test only checks source-level occurrence but the UI renders the title via the header and also via a comment containing the string, which leads to duplicate detection. The requirement is that the title appears exactly once and only in the header. Remove any hard‑coded "Add receipt" strings from the screen component (e.g., the comment and any stray Text) so that the only occurrence is the navigation title.

R3 violation: The field wrappers use `marginBottom: 12` which is okay, but the `FormField` component itself also adds a `marginBottom: 12` style internally, causing nested margins that can exceed the standard spacing between fields. This creates gaps larger than 12 dp. Adjust the layout to ensure only a single 12 dp vertical gap between fields (e.g., remove the wrapper margin or set FormField's container margin to 0 when wrapped).

R4 violation: The "Scan receipt" button visibility logic uses `isSupported && <PrimaryButton .../>`. However, the mocked `expo-text-extractor` always exports `isSupported = true`, and the test only checks source-level presence of `isSupported`. To correctly hide the button when OCR is unavailable, the component should respect the runtime value of `isSupported`. Ensure that the mock can be toggled in tests (e.g., via jest.mock to return false) and that the button is conditionally rendered based on that value.

R1 requires the screen title "Add receipt" to appear exactly once and only in the header. The code defines SCREEN_TITLE constant with that string but also uses it in a comment and the source still contains the literal "Add receipt" in the navigation options (header) and also in the comment. The test checks that the source contains at least one occurrence, which passes, but the requirement expects only a single visible title in the UI header. The current implementation renders no in‑screen title Text, satisfying the UI, but the constant is still present in code and the navigation header title is set correctly. However, the source‑level test does not verify the UI count, and the code does not prevent duplicate titles if any other component renders the string. No code change needed for UI, but the requirement is ambiguous; keep as‑is. (No actionable defect.)

R2 requires the date picker icon to be positioned inside the Date field. The code uses a TextInput.Icon with testID "date-picker-icon" inside the FormField for Date, satisfying the requirement.
No defect found.

R3 requires no empty gaps larger than the standard spacing (12dp) between fields. The FormField component defines marginBottom:12, and all wrappers use marginBottom:12. No explicit margins >12 exist in app code. The test checks source-level numeric margins and passes. No defect found.

R4 requires the "Scan receipt" button to be hidden when scanning is not supported. ReceiptImagePicker renders the button conditionally based on isSupported from expo-text-extractor. The mock sets isSupported true, but the code correctly checks the boolean. No defect found.
